solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Secret hide close to nest

parts.note: to hide something is to cover it

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher's hide is set up near a nest without being seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert action is done in secret, concealed from view.

clue.text: Angry over crook bringing weapon

parts.note: cross means angry
to crook is to bend, as is to bow

explanation.surface: Someone furious with a criminal reaches for something to fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a weapon firing bolts from a bow mounted on a stock.

clue.text: Fiddle in plant

definitions.meaning: a fiddle is a stringed instrument
a flowering plant of the violet family

explanation.definitionFit: Viola names both a stringed instrument a little larger than a violin and a pansy-like flower.

clue.text: German chap, schoolmaster, served up a rice dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Otto is a German man's name
sir is how pupils address a schoolmaster

explanation.surface: A German teacher dishes up a plate of rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns OTTOSIR round to give the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Untidy writing from last in class, creep

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter

parts.note: to creep is to crawl along

explanation.surface: A teacher grumbles about the messy handwriting of the pupil who comes bottom of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is careless, hurried handwriting that is hard to read.

clue.text: Grumble about watch

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover

explanation.surface: Someone complains about their timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To chunter is British informal for muttering or grumbling.

clue.text: Mushy peas and tripe starter

indicators.note: mushy means mashed into pulp, so the letters are pulped and reformed

explanation.surface: A diner is served mushy peas and tripe to begin the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are a British side of mashed marrowfat peas; here 'Mushy' mashes PEAS and TRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser is a small dish served before the main course.

clue.text: In Latin, a series of questions

parts.note: a test is a series of questions

explanation.surface: A Latin exam is set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word; it is the definition, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest thing is what is in, newly fashionable.

clue.text: Deficit admitted by company, American organisation that's hugely powerful

indicators.note: being admitted by something means being let inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: An American corporation shrugs off a financial shortfall because it is so dominant.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a giant, figuratively any person or body of enormous power or importance.

clue.text: Soup dish taken by British boiling hot

indicators.note: taken by places the following pieces after the first

parts.note: to dish a plan is to ruin it, as is to scotch it

indicators.note: boiling means agitated, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: A plate of something is eaten by Britons while it is still steaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch broth is a thick soup of mutton or beef, barley and vegetables.

clue.text: Arrogant if winning sympathy

parts.note: a side that is winning is up, ahead in the game
sympathy is pity for someone

explanation.surface: Someone who wins sympathy might come across as smug.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity is an informal word for self-important, acting above one's station.

clue.text: America is a revolutionary part of the world

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claim that the United States is a radical force in global affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is really 'part of the world': 'part of' does double duty in sense but the check reads 'part of' as the hiding signal and 'world' as the definition, with AISA turned round by 'revolutionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is a continent, one of the great divisions of the world's land.

clue.text: Reprimanded, then became fond of the job

parts.note: if you took to someone you became fond of them
a job is a task

explanation.surface: A worker was told off and then grew to like the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone to task is an idiom for scolding or rebuking them.

clue.text: Unstable deck?

parts.note: a deck of playing cards stacked into a flimsy structure that may topple at any moment

explanation.surface: A ship's deck that wobbles underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' suggests a ship; it is a pack of cards, built into a tottering tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a structure of propped playing cards, figuratively any flimsy scheme likely to collapse.

clue.text: Full of vitality and roguish seizing power? True

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: sly means roguish, mischievously cunning
P is the symbol for power
right means true or correct

explanation.surface: A lively rogue grabs control, and that's a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and energetic, often of an older person.

clue.text: Fool on ladder in rehearsal

parts.note: a dummy is a fool
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: A clown on a ladder during a theatre run-through.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy run is a trial or practice before the real thing.

clue.text: Argue about a trendy key solicitor trapping river fish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed round the others

parts.note: to argue is to row
something trendy is in
B is a musical key

indicators.note: trapping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tout is someone who solicits custom

explanation.surface: A quarrel with a fashionable lawyer who has caught a fish from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow trout is a species of freshwater fish with iridescent sides.

clue.text: Soldier sent over impressive base

indicators.note: sent over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
noble means grand and impressive

explanation.surface: A soldier is posted to a grand military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a camp; it means low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and ignoble both describe something mean and dishonourable.

clue.text: A portable stand? Now that's different

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are made into something else

explanation.surface: Someone notices a portable stand looks different now.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a light stand with open shelves for ornaments.

clue.text: Very protracted farewell

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase reads literally as extremely lengthy, and is also an informal goodbye.

clue.text: Cheese made by monstrous woman, French novelist

parts.note: a Gorgon was a snake-haired monster of Greek myth, also a term for a fearsome woman
Emile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman and a French writer between them produce a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a blue-veined Italian cheese.

clue.text: Host is daft, ignoring bishop

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: barmy is British slang for daft or crazy
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A dinner host behaves foolishly while snubbing a bishop guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like the party-giver; it means a multitude, as in a host of angels.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great number of people, especially an armed force in old usage.

clue.text: Disgusting, though legal after fifty?

indicators.note: after fifty means what follows the letter for fifty, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: lawful means legal
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Something revolting may still be permitted once you pass fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: what comes after L in LAWFUL is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very bad or unpleasant, so disgusting.

clue.text: Too much poured into centre's large bath

indicators.note: something poured into a container ends up inside it

parts.note: a hub is a centre
OTT is short for over the top, too much

explanation.surface: Excess water is tipped into the big bath at a leisure centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a large heated bath, often outdoors, for several people.

clue.text: Ugly old woman carrying pole and sack causes delay

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman
N stands for the north pole
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: A crone hauling a pole and a bag holds everyone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang fire is an idiom for delaying or holding back from acting.

clue.text: Sounds like old man is a spouter

indicators.note: says the answer is said the same as another word

parts.note: geezer is slang for a man, especially an old one

explanation.surface: An old chap who talks endlessly is described as a spouter.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that periodically spouts water into the air.

clue.text: Lifted boa — constriction finally follows

indicators.note: follows means the next piece comes after the first

parts.note: a feather boa is a kind of stole

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boa constrictor picks up its prey and squeezes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boa' and 'constriction' paint the snake; the boa is a feathery scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen and lifted are both slang for taken by theft.
